precepts.text: I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, and will put my words in his mouth. Whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him: meaning he will cut you off.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Moses himself foretold Christ: “I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.” That Prophet is Christ.

“And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.” Meaning he'll kill you; he'll cut you off. That is what the Lord is saying.

So those who held on to animal sacrifice and refused the words of Christ were refusing the very Prophet Moses spoke of. The law they claimed to defend told them to hearken to him, and he is the one who blotted out the ordinances and nailed them to his cross.

precepts.text: There shall not be found among you any one that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits. This is the commandment Saul turned around and broke.
precepts.point: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and came to the woman by night. And the woman said, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

precepts.why:
This is the commandment Saul turned around and broke: “There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits.” The Lord said none of these would be found among Israel.

Saul had just rid the land of all of them: the soothsayers, the witches, the familiar spirits and the wizards. That is what the woman at En-dor throws back at him: “thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?” You trying to get me killed.

Now the Lord has stopped answering him, “neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets”, and the same man who cut them off says, “Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her.” Find me a wizard so I can know what is going on. His mind is all over the place. He is double-minded, breaking the very commandment he had enforced, and he disguises himself and goes by night so no one will see it.

That is where bashfulness leads: self-willed, disobedient, deceitful, making excuses, easily manipulated. Samuel tells him the Lord “is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” The Lord rent the kingdom out of his hand and gave it to David, and Saul and his sons would be with Samuel the next day. “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness.” Saul never believed in himself, so he never believed God; he had Samuel's counsel the whole time and would not listen, and when that guidance was gone he ran to the very thing the law forbade.

precepts.text: I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, and will put my words in his mouth: called an angel in one book and the prophet in another, and both are Christ.
precepts.point: For my name is in him means they share the same titles.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee: Christ, not Joshua, fulfilled this word.
precepts.point: None matched all the signs and the wonders which the Lord sent Moses to do in the land of Egypt, and all that mighty hand, and all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel. With this the Torah, the books of Moses, is finished.

note.label: Deuteronomy 34: The Death of Moses

precepts.why:
“I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.” This is what makes Deuteronomy 34:10 heavy, because of a doctrine: some say Joshua was the prophet raised up like unto Moses, and therefore there is no Christ.

But the scripture that acknowledges Joshua rising up with the spirit upon him says in the same breath, “there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face”. Joshua was a mighty prophet, but he did not fit that word. None matched “all the signs and the wonders, which the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt”, “all that mighty hand”, and “all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel.”

Christ did. Christ, not Joshua, fulfilled this word: the Prophet like unto Moses, with the words of the Most High put in his mouth, speaking all that he was commanded. With this the Torah, the books of Moses, is finished.

precepts.text: Whosoever will not hearken unto the words of the Lord, he will require it of him; the Lord requires it whenever you go off.
precepts.point: If we built an altar to turn from following the Lord, or to offer burnt offerings, meat offerings, or peace offerings on it, let the Lord himself require it.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

precepts.why:
The two and a half tribes put their own lives on the line: “if it be in rebellion, or if in transgression against the Lord, (save us not this day,)”. If we built this thing in rebellion, put us to death today. And if it was to turn from following the Lord or to offer burnt offering, meat offering or peace offerings on it, “let the Lord himself require it”.

Require it is the Lord's own word: “And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.” The Lord requires it whenever you go off. So they call on the Lord God of gods, who knoweth, to require it of them himself if the altar was anything other than what they said.

precepts.text: The test of a true prophet is that the thing he speaks in the name of the Most High comes to pass.
precepts.point: He gives a sign: the altar will be rent and its ashes poured out. When Jeroboam stretches out his hand to have him seized, that hand dries up and cannot be pulled back, and the altar is rent as the sign declared.

note.label: 1 Kings 13: The Man of God and the Two Prophets

precepts.why:
“But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.” And how shall we know? “When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken”. The test of a true prophet is that the thing he speaks in the name of the Most High comes to pass.

The man of God out of Judah passed that test. He cried against Jeroboam's altar in Bethel that a child of the house of David, “Josiah by name”, would offer the priests of the high places upon it, “and men’s bones shall be burnt upon thee.” He gave a sign the same day: “Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.”

When Jeroboam put forth his hand, saying, “Lay hold on him”, his hand “dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him.” “The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.” It came to pass, so the word was from the Most High.

precepts.text: Israel is forbidden to use divination, enchantment, or to consult with familiar spirits.
precepts.point: The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 10: The Death of Saul

precepts.why:
The law is plain: “There shall not be found among you any one” that “useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch”, nor “a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.” Israel is forbidden to use divination, enchantment, or to consult with familiar spirits.

Saul died “for his transgression which he committed against the Lord, even against the word of the Lord, which he kept not, and also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it”. That was the last straw for him. The left hand of the Most High is real, and people who meddle with it get entangled and get spirits put on them. It is not our custom.

precepts.text: The law forbids passing a son or daughter through the fire, divination, observing times, enchantment, witchcraft, familiar spirits, and necromancy, and commands to be perfect with the Most High.
precepts.point: He sets a carved idol in the house of God, the very house of which the Most High said to David and Solomon, In this house and in Jerusalem will I put my name for ever, and Manasseh makes Judah do worse than the heathen the Lord destroyed before them.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. For all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord”. And: “Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God.”

Manasseh did every one of them: “he caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom: also he observed times, and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards”. Every one of these things is a commandment he broke. Passing children through the fire is child sacrifice, the same spirit as abortion today.

The law says “because of these abominations the Lord thy God doth drive them out from before thee.” Manasseh brought those same abominations into the house of the Lord: he “built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord”, and “wrought much evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.”

precepts.text: A Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me.
precepts.point: What he came to fulfil is the prophecies written concerning him, not the commandments given to Israel to keep. Everything in chapter 2 of this same gospel is an example of that fulfilling.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
Moses wrote of him in the law: “The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken”.

Christ is that Prophet raised up from the midst of Israel, of their brethren, like unto Moses. This is one of the things written in the law of Moses concerning him, and his coming fulfilled it. It is a prophecy to be brought to pass, not a commandment to be destroyed.

precepts.text: "I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth," the passage Peter quotes.
precepts.point: Peter is quoting Moses, and every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
This is the passage Peter is quoting: “I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.”

Peter is quoting Moses. Every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept.

The prophet is raised up from among their brethren, meaning from among men. That proves Christ came through the seed of a man, not immaculate conception. And the Most High put his words in his mouth, which is why every soul that will not hear that prophet is destroyed from among the people.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Two separate brothers found books of witchcraft their wives were using on them. “That maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire”: killing your children, what we call abortions today. “Or an observer of times”: horoscopes, Capricorn, Leo, Sagittarius. “Or a charmer”: lucky charms and amulets. “Or a consulter with familiar spirits”: they conjure up your dead uncle. “Or a necromancer”: somebody that talks with the dead. “For all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 22

precepts.why: Sorcerers: the coconut under somebody’s bed, the tarot cards, the Ouija board. “That maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire”: that is abortion, killing your babies. “Or that useth divination”: rolling bones on the floor. “Or an observer of times”: the horoscope. “Or an enchanter”: casting spells on people. “Or a witch”: a female. “Or a charmer”: the lucky charm, the rabbit’s foot, the four-leaf clover. “Or a consulter with familiar spirits”: like the movie Ghost, your dead aunt has a message for you. “Or a wizard”: the male version. “Or a necromancer”: someone that talks with the dead, like the woman who raised up Samuel.
